source.citation: Krutyanskiy et al., Telecom-Wavelength Quantum Repeater Node Based on a Trapped-Ion Processor, Physical Review Letters 130, 213601 (2023)
source.parameter_location: main text and Supplementary Sections II--IV

validity.distance_semantics: distance between neighboring ion nodes; the photonic Bell station is at the midpoint
validity.route_scope: component-based extrapolation only; a multi-node chain with these current parameters was not demonstrated

hardware.resource_semantics: one trapped ion per adjacent link in the two-ion node; no unbounded pool provisioning

rate_model.approximation_uncertainty: the source states that the inherited nesting expression is approximate to within a factor 1.5

state_model.elementary_channel: phase-error Bell mixture from Supplementary Eqs. S13--S14
state_model.local_swap_channel: single-output-qubit depolarizing map from Supplementary Eq. S15

storage_decoherence_model.coherence_time_definition: Gaussian fit parameter measured with neighboring-ion photon-generation attempts active
storage_decoherence_model.source: main text Fig. 4 and Supplementary Eq. S11

memory_model.decay_semantics: the stored spin-qubit states have no natural spontaneous-decay rate in this protocol; storage error is modeled as Gaussian dephasing

controller_model.scheduling: parallel adjacent-link generation, storage of the first success, and local deterministic Bell swapping

notes: The numerical parameters are demonstrated in one two-ion repeater node, including a 128-fold memory enhancement and 5.9 Hz absolute repeater delivery over two 25 km fibers. Applying them to a chain is a demonstrated-component extrapolation, not a demonstrated multi-node system. The profile intentionally has one slot per adjacent edge side; it must never be used to synthesize dozens of independent memories merely to hit a requested route-availability target.
